notes: Programmatically checked for any column that is both integer-typed and 100% unique-valued (a plausible row-ID). Result: no explicit identifier/row-ID column exists in the raw data.
Ratio of largest class count to smallest class count -> confirms imbalance.
Detected via regex PIR_\d+: PIR_1 ... PIR_55

Temperature==0 is not physically plausible for an indoor office in deg F and is treated as a probable sensor-dropout / missing-value sentinel. DECISION: these rows are NOT silently imputed (to avoid leaking distributional information from the full dataset into any train fold); a boolean flag column 'Temperature_F_is_zero_flag' is added in preprocessing so downstream models can (optionally) treat it as informative missingness, and the raw value is otherwise left untouched.
Fraction of consecutive-observation gaps exceeding 60 seconds -> evidence sampling is NOT perfectly evenly spaced (confirms task note).
More than 1 unique gap value confirms non-uniform sampling interval.

Raw Date/Time strings are exact timestamps; used only to build temporal groups for StratifiedGroupKFold and for the temporal stress test, and are EXCLUDED from the model feature matrix to prevent the model from memorizing timestamps.
No column is both unique-valued and an unambiguous row identifier; row order in the CSV is the only implicit identifier and is not used as a feature.
